epic.title: cleanup-a-door — make the MCP door usable by the session that needs it
epic.intent_and_why: An orchestrator could not bind the door to a spine it was about to create, so every epic since #424 drove its own spine through the CLI — the opposite of what #559 ruled.

definition_of_done: A session started with no SPINE_FILE calls spine_open, gets bound, and drives a real spine end to end without touching the CLI.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: The identity guard is not weakened while it is made reachable
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Subprocess probes plus committed regression tests that fail pre-fix

hard_constraints: No tool takes a spine path per call
checklist_engine.py, scripts/hooks/**, run_crew.py, gauge_reader.py belong to lanes B and C

current_wave.objective: Fix #604, #605 and #603 so the door is usable

completed_outcomes.outcome: The door fails closed when unbound and spine_open binds the calling process, so a session that starts unbound can mint work and drive it.
completed_outcomes.evidence: Reproduced in one process: unbound refused by name, spine_open returned SPINE_FILE and SPINE_SESSION, spine_lease claim succeeded. tests/test_mcp_lifecycle.py:194 byte-identical (zero removed lines vs a69bbac4) with a stronger module-wide assignment pin added; tests/test_mcp_door_unbound.py fails 12/12 on a reverted server.
